These do not involve command substitution or external network calls.

The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum and is not set to `'SKIP'`, so there is no issue with source verification at this stage. Even if it were skipped, that would not affect the safety of `--printsrcinfo`. The source URL points to a release asset on GitHub matching the declared upstream project, and while it uses variable expansion, it does not involve dynamic fetching or execution during sourcing. There is no evidence of obfuscated code, data exfiltration, or remote code execution during parse time.

All constructs are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices. No malicious behavior is possible during the `makepkg --printsrcinfo` phase because no code is executed beyond sourcing the file, and the file contains no dangerous top-level logic.
</details>
